column1: # Hand-written translation query answers, merged over the generated shader_facts.tsv by shader_split.py.
# Each row is  key <TAB> {"tex":{"<slot>":"<type>"}}  (types: 2d 2darray cube cubearray 3d buffer 1d 1darray 2dms 2dmsarray).
# STATUS 2026-11-08: an answer-table "tex" row cannot change an Ampere texture's type. These two rows were
# tried at slot 0, at slot 1 and at both, and are inert by construction; they are kept only as the record of
# the test, and are safe to delete.
#   - The job document carries the row. DM_JOB_DUMP=<dir> (dmsh_build.py xl()) copies the job the translator
#     receives, and d92d9b75e2cc7dad's document reads "tex": {"0":"3d","1":"3d"} -- so Program.cs's
#     _job["tex"][slot.ToString()] has the value it looks for. The writer and the reader agree.
#   - The emitted type still does not change: the rebuilt chain 4af3b2a70fef's d92d9b75e2cc7dad_b.metal has
#     3 texture2d and 0 texture3d, and the bind-time mismatch survives.
#   - Why: the Ampere sample (InstEmitAmpereMem.cs ATex) takes its type from the instruction's own dimension
#     field -- TexDim dim = ATexDim(context, x.Bits(61, 64)) -- and never calls QuerySamplerType. The answer
#     table reaches a texture type only through the Maxwell TEX path (InstEmitTexture.cs:1140), bindless
#     handles and TXQ. So for a Switch 2 shader the row is dead on arrival.
# What the mismatch really is: the shader declares slot 0 as 2D because its instruction says 2D (dim 1), and
# the game binds a 3D texture there (NVN target 2, Metal type 7). The shader is not asking for a 3D read.
# The host's tex_fit bridges "wants 3D, holds 2D" and "wants 2D, holds cube" but has no "wants 2D, holds 3D"
# case, so it falls through to tex_mis_note("bound as is"). The open question is the dimension field's
# correctness against NAK's sm70_encode.rs, and whether the host should make a 2D view of the 3D texture.
# See docs/SWITCH2.md, "The answer table's tex row never reaches an Ampere texture".
